accentPalettes.storage: one shared preset per space in space.yml, owner-written through PATCH /api/spaces/{space}; the v0.4 browser-local key seeds it once, then is deleted
accentPalettes.contrastFloor: 4.5:1 accent-on-ground, ink-on-accent and body ink on the composited 12% wash over ground, inset, surface and raised in both schemes, enforced by web/src/lib/accent.test.ts

surfaces.spaceCover: Three bands on one ground: a masthead under a hairline (space icon at 40px, name at --text-display with the mono tracking, one factual line — types, records, members, role — and a thumb row holding Open schedule as a ghost button and Capture a record as the primary), the body, and a colophon. The body is a keyed type ledger (icon, name, mono key in a 5rem column, the record count in the type's own plural, a Scheduled label, a quiet arrow; the whole row links) that closes with a quiet New type row. At xl the five most recently written records sit in a 4/12 margin behind a hairline: icon, title, a mono type · time-ago line, and the keys the last write changed (past three, a +N count); it collapses beneath the ledger below xl, and a space with no writes renders no margin so the ledger takes all 12 columns. Under the body, a Graph band draws the whole space with the record count at the trailing edge and no centre ring. The colophon reads space.yml · timezone · space key on the leading edge and Settings on the trailing edge.
surfaces.spaceIndex: The all-spaces page opens with the cover masthead grammar: Spaces in the display face, one sentence naming what a space is, the count at the trailing edge, then the keyed ledger (key, name, members, types, role) and the create form under a visible label.
surfaces.commandPalette: Bottom sheet below sm, 40rem centred above; one search row and grouped results in server order for records, with the matching sentence as a second line; 44px rows on coarse pointers; keyboard footer only on keyboard screens; focus trapped and returned.
surfaces.quickCapture: Two-mode sheet, 34rem wide; type, title, required properties only; Create keeps the sheet, Create and open navigates; refusals stay inline with Retry.
surfaces.bulkBar: Hairline band inside the table scrollport, not a floating card; names count and property, previews the value, keeps failed rows selected, Undo runs from the page.
surfaces.rowActions: Line icons at one weight; 32px fine pointer, 44px coarse; phones fold Complete/Duplicate/Trash into one 44px menu and keep Open separate.
surfaces.spaceRail: A 13rem rail on desktop and the same rows in the phone sheet: All spaces, Overview, five utility links and Types, each a 14px row with a 14px line icon, muted at rest and ink on hover. The current page is ink text behind a 2px accent rule at the row's leading edge, never a filled chip. Reorder reveals 32px up/down pairs (44px coarse) and the order persists per user and space in the browser.
surfaces.mobileSheets: Palette, capture, space drawer and row menu rise from the bottom on one visual-viewport geometry (--vv-top/--vv-height, written from visualViewport): every sheet ends above the on-screen keyboard, even on iOS where the layout viewport does not shrink. The last row carries safe-area padding; 180ms rise and fade in, 120ms fade out, static under reduced motion; focus trap; Escape and a close control; content and footer reserve room for the fixed space bar.
surfaces.tablePhones: Below 640px the checkbox and title are pinned at the left (136px), property columns paint 104px and swipe in one document scroller with the thead stuck to the top, and a trailing spacer lets the last column clear the opaque 56px action rail. No resize handles on a coarse pointer; Select preserves scrollLeft; the header drops the mono key line.
surfaces.recordPhone: The title input owns its line at 26px; the sticky save bar is the only save indicator; the id and revision sit behind one mono disclosure (last six characters, full id plus copy); one UPDATED line; a property's mono key echo is hidden below sm.
surfaces.recordLinks: A resolved [[Type/Title]] reads as its title with the accent underline and opens in place; an unknown or ambiguous target uses a dotted warning underline and a title, never a navigation; code spans and fences stay literal; an unsaved valid link reads as plain text until saved.
surfaces.bodyEditor: One hairline toolbar above a textarea edits only text: bold, italic, inline code, an H1–H3 heading menu, lists, quote and the two link tools; 32px fine and 44px coarse. On a phone the controls form two rows of six columns, ending with Save. Write is a split from lg up with the read renderer beside it; below lg one pane and a Write/Preview switch, with the textarea kept mounted so undo and selection survive. On a coarse pointer Write becomes a fixed writing sheet against the visual viewport: the page, navigation and page save bar step aside, Save lives in the toolbar, a visible Done action and Escape close the sheet, and the textarea scrolls inside it. Done returns the page at its prior scroll. Typing and toolbar edits keep the caret in view, with three lines of lower margin and a re-check while Safari settles the keyboard. / and [[ share one caret popup clamped to the visual viewport; Enter or Tab accepts, Space never does, and a slash command opens only at line start outside a fence. A live type prefix turns an unresolved [[type/Title into a trailing Create row. Pasting one URL over a selection makes a markdown link; tapping non-link preview prose enters Write at the end.
surfaces.linksPanel: Below the body and above history: a mono count across both directions, Links to rows (outgoing relations with Type · via Property, then outgoing mentions with Type · mentioned in this body), Linked from rows (type glyph, source title, Type · via Property), and Mentioned in rows (title, type name, two-line snippet, ×N). A group renders only when non-empty; the whole row navigates, 44px on a coarse pointer; empty is one sentence naming relation properties and [[Type/Title]].
surfaces.graph: A full-width Graph row, closed by default, shown whenever either direction has a link, above a drawing capped at 44rem with Local/Space scope and a solid-relation / dashed-mention legend. The local map draws outgoing and incoming edges from the same rows the panel lists. Local rings hold 24 nodes (12 inner) and the space map places every live record by degree. Nodes are links with accent focus rings and the centre is aria-current; wheel zoom runs 0.6x to 2.6x and a drag pans or moves one node with its edges. On a touch pointer a drag anywhere always pans and never moves a node, while a tap opens the record; node dragging stays a mouse or pen gesture, and page scrolling starts outside the drawing. Offsets are view-only and reset when the record or scope changes; the drawing never mirrors, only the zoom controls follow the thumb edge.
surfaces.sheetGeometry: .sheet-viewport is fixed against the visual viewport, bottom-aligned below sm and a 12vh-top centred dialog above; .sheet-popup is capped at --vv-height minus a margin; no overlay uses inset:0 or 100dvh; viewport-fit=cover makes env(safe-area-inset-*) real.
surfaces.addProperty: A ruled dialog from the trailing table header or the Columns panel: an existing library property or a new name and format; property, type member (featured) and current-view column write in order, staying open with a named stage and Retry on failure. Editor-only, no wizard, one toast on success.
surfaces.recordIcons: One optional user-authored emoji in frontmatter (schema 4), never a property or interface icon. A fixed slot in the record header, table title cell, home recents, palette results, board cards, gallery tiles and Trash; absent means no empty box.
surfaces.sheetClose: Right-handed keeps the platform-standard trailing close; left-handed puts the same control first in the title or search row, with focus order and margin following the DOM.
surfaces.searchLanding: Opening a record from a search result keeps ?q= in the address. MarkdownView marks every rendered occurrence with the accent and scrolls the first one into view once after the preview paints, without stealing focus. The body header shows Match: “<query>” with a clear control that removes q via replace so Back returns to the search. Code and fences stay unmarked, and re-opening the same query does not fight a reader's scroll.
surfaces.renameRepair: A title change on a record with inbound body mentions opens one preview dialog before the write: old and new title, each source with its type and mention count, and Update links / Rename only / Cancel. Sources are read while the old title still resolves. Update links renames first, then rewrites only occurrences that resolved to the record before the rename, each through an ordinary source PATCH; a stale source is skipped and reported, never retried. Rename only leaves old mentions unresolved; Cancel writes nothing. The dialog uses the sheet geometry and its action row follows the thumb edge.
surfaces.accountMenu: One labelled menu closes the header row: the trigger carries the account glyph and the signed-in email at sm and up, and opens a 15rem popup with Account settings and Sign out. Arrow keys rove the items, Escape closes it, and a cancelled sign-out returns focus to the trigger because the item that opened it has unmounted.
surfaces.foundation: Six type roles with Maple Mono for display, title and every mono role over IBM Plex Sans body; the neutral scale adds Night Inset below the ground; one 12% accent wash marks selection, the active row and the search match; 4px spacing scale; 36/40/44 control heights and 40/44 fields; 120/180/240ms motion on one exponential ease-out.

display.purpose: Space name, auth and page titles; Maple Mono 36/1.05 with -0.03em, 30/1.08 on a phone, ligatures off.

title.purpose: Record title and type page name; Maple Mono 26/1.1 with -0.02em, 22/1.15 on a phone.

body.purpose: Prose, form values and row names; IBM Plex Sans 15/1.6.

label.purpose: Column headers, field labels, roles and keys; uppercase Maple Mono 11/1.5, 0.09em.

small.purpose: Secondary rows, hints, metadata sentences and errors; IBM Plex Sans 13/1.5.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: One exponential ease-out for every entrance and state transition.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Result changes, hover colour and palette result entrance.

motion.name: base
motion.purpose: Every overlay entrance and the sheet rise.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: One entrance on a page's main content; fill-mode backwards so a fixed descendant is never trapped in a wrapper; removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: sheet
motion.purpose: One entrance for every overlay; static under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one stateful action on a view: sign in, create account, create space.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; min-height:var(--control-standard,40px); padding:10px 16px; border:0; border-radius:var(--radius-field,6px); background:var(--color-accent,#c8d96b); color:var(--color-accent-ink,#14180f); font-family:var(--font-sans,'IBM Plex Sans Variable',system-ui,sans-serif); font-size:13px; font-weight:500; cursor:pointer; transition:filter var(--duration-fast,120ms) var(--ease-out,cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter:brightness(1.05); } .ds-btn-primary:active { filter:brightness(.95); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--color-accent,#c8d96b); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled, .ds-btn-primary[data-loading] { opacity:.5; cursor:not-allowed; } .ds-btn-primary[aria-busy=true] { cursor:wait; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary action: sign out, retry, cancel.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; min-height:var(--control-standard,40px); padding:10px 16px; border:1px solid var(--color-line-interactive,#667066); border-radius:var(--radius-field,6px); background:transparent; color:var(--color-ink,#e8ece4); font-family:var(--font-sans,'IBM Plex Sans Variable',system-ui,sans-serif); font-size:13px; font-weight:500; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color var(--duration-fast,120ms) var(--ease-out,cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)), border-color var(--duration-fast,120ms) var(--ease-out,cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background:var(--color-raised,#212621); border-color:var(--color-line-strong,#3a423a); } .ds-btn-ghost:active { background:var(--color-inset,#0d100d); } .ds-btn-ghost[aria-pressed=true] { background:var(--color-accent-wash,#c8d96b1e); border-color:var(--color-accent,#c8d96b); color:var(--color-accent,#c8d96b); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--color-accent,#c8d96b); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Quiet Button
components.description: Borderless secondary action in a dense row or overlay footer.
components.css: .ds-btn-quiet { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; min-height:var(--control-standard,40px); padding:10px 16px; border:1px solid transparent; border-radius:var(--radius-field,6px); background:transparent; color:var(--color-muted,#9aa398); font-family:var(--font-sans,'IBM Plex Sans Variable',system-ui,sans-serif); font-size:13px; font-weight:500; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color var(--duration-fast,120ms) var(--ease-out,cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)), color var(--duration-fast,120ms) var(--ease-out,cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)); } .ds-btn-quiet:hover { background:var(--color-raised,#212621); color:var(--color-ink,#e8ece4); } .ds-btn-quiet[aria-pressed=true] { background:var(--color-accent-wash,#c8d96b1e); color:var(--color-accent,#c8d96b); } .ds-btn-quiet:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--color-accent,#c8d96b); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: A destructive action whose label names the loss; ember border and text, never a filled red.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; min-height:var(--control-standard,40px); padding:10px 16px; border:1px solid var(--color-danger,#f08a72); border-radius:var(--radius-field,6px); background:transparent; color:var(--color-danger,#f08a72); font-family:var(--font-sans,'IBM Plex Sans Variable',system-ui,sans-serif); font-size:13px; font-weight:500; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color var(--duration-fast,120ms) var(--ease-out,cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)); } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background:var(--color-raised,#212621); } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--color-accent,#c8d96b); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Primitive States
components.description: Hover, focus-visible, active, selected, disabled, loading, error and read-only are defined once in components/ui/controls.tsx. Focus is a 2px accent outline with 2px offset on every control; errors are ember border plus a role=alert message, never colour alone.
components.css: .ds-focus { outline:2px solid var(--color-accent,#c8d96b); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-disabled { opacity:.5; cursor:not-allowed; } .ds-invalid { border-color:var(--color-danger,#f08a72); } .ds-selected { background:var(--color-accent-wash,#c8d96b1e); color:var(--color-accent,#c8d96b); }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Labeled input with hint and error slots.

components.name: App Header
components.description: The signed-in navigation: wordmark at left, account and sign-out at right.
components.html: thingyou@example.com

components.name: Space Index Entry
components.description: The signature row: mono key, name, counts, role, and an annotation that opens beneath it.
components.html: Garden10OWNER

narrative.overview: The interface is a field index read under a headlamp: dark ground, hairline rules, keys in mono, annotations in the margin. It treats the user's data the way a naturalist treats a specimen sheet — the record is the subject; the apparatus around it stays small, aligned and quiet. The product is a working tool first. The v0.5.2 foundation adds a display mono voice (Maple Mono), a six-step type scale, one accent wash, a 4px space scale and named primitive states. The world still contributes type, palette, density and one signature move (the keyed entry), never the navigation model or the controls.
keyCharacteristics: Dark ground with near-neutral, slightly green-black surfaces and one inset step below the ground.
Hairline 1px rules instead of shadows or cards.
Maple Mono for display, page titles, the wordmark, keys, ids, timestamps, counts and labels; IBM Plex Sans for prose, controls and tables.
One accent per space, chosen by an owner from six contrast-tested palettes and shared by every member, used only for state; one 12% accent wash is the only tint.
A keyed index as the recurring structure: a short mono key leads every entry.
A real margin at xl for annotations, counts and properties; motion explains change and is absent under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The chosen accent (Lichen by default) marks state: focus, selection, the primary action, the wordmark, the active rail and view tabs. An owner sets it once for the space; every member sees it. It never fills large areas and never appears twice in one row for two different meanings. Choosing another palette does not add a second accent.

rules.name: The Light Is Not a Theme Skin Rule
rules.body: Light mode keeps the same type scale, rules and hierarchy. It swaps the ground to bone and darkens the accent for contrast; it does not add shadows, cards or new ornament.

rules.name: The Keys Are Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything the system treats as an identifier or measurement is mono and tabular. Anything a person reads as a sentence is sans.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: A divider is 1px of line. Never a 2px border, never a colored side stripe, never a shadow standing in for a rule.

rules.name: The Keyboard Is Part of the Layout Rule
rules.body: Every overlay positions against the visual viewport (--vv-height/--vv-top from visualViewport), never against inset:0 or 100dvh, so no sheet, footer or sticky save bar can end under the on-screen keyboard. A focusable field that opens a sheet takes focus in the same commit so a phone raises the keyboard on the first tap. Toasts follow the same geometry: on a phone the stack sits above the bar, and above the keyboard when it is up.

rules.name: The 11px Floor Rule
rules.body: No functional text is smaller than 11px; the only 10px step is the mono property-key echo under a fine-pointer table header, and that line is removed on a phone. Coarse pointers get 16px inputs so focusing one never zooms the page, and 44x44 targets.

rules.name: The Thumb First Rule
rules.body: Below lg the rail and every overlay rise from the bottom of the screen, with 44px targets and safe-area padding. A keyboard shortcut that has no keyboard is not rendered. A compact editor's primary action sits at the thumb edge: last in the DOM at the right edge by default and first in the DOM at the left edge in left-handed mode, with clear/cancel before it on the right and after it on the left. The row reverses in the DOM so paint, Tab and screen-reader order agree. Dialog and sheet close controls follow the same handedness; the platform-standard trailing close is the right-handed default.

rules.name: The Picker Browses Rule
rules.body: On a compact width or a coarse pointer the emoji picker is a bottom sheet on the visual-viewport geometry, opened in front of whatever form called it, never a popover anchored above the trigger. It opens without raising the keyboard and focuses its own popup so the grid gets the screen; tapping its search field raises the keyboard and the sheet shrinks above it. Above sm with a fine pointer it stays the anchored popover.

rules.name: The Recents Lead Rule
rules.body: The picker leads with the last eight glyphs chosen in this browser, and opening scrolls the current icon into view without scrolling while a search filters the grid. Recents are a UI preference, never space content, and the custom field accepts multi-part emoji up to 32 code units.

rules.name: The Five Controls Rule
rules.body: Below sm the type toolbar is five 44px controls on one row: search, Filter, Sort, Columns and View, with Columns absent on a calendar. View opens one sheet whose first screen is a menu of View settings, Save as view and CSV, each panel returning through Back. A changed query or view shows one labelled band under the toolbar with Save and Reset; the band never wraps.

rules.name: The Mono Is a Voice Rule
rules.body: Maple Mono sets display and page titles, the record title and one pull-quote or empty-state line per surface, at 400 with negative tracking and contextual alternates off so a title shows the characters it was given. Body, controls, tables and prose stay sans; keys, counts, dates and annotations stay mono. A monospaced paragraph is a defect.

rules.name: The One Wash Rule
rules.body: The accent wash is the only tint in the system: the chosen accent at 12% alpha, for selection, the active row, the search match and drag. It is never a decorative panel, a gradient or a second accent, and body ink on the composited wash stays at 4.5:1 or better over ground, inset, surface and raised in both schemes.

rules.name: The Margin Rule
rules.body: At xl the composed pages use a real margin column for annotations, counts, folios and properties. The margin is information, not decoration; if it has nothing to say, it collapses into the reading order.

rules.name: The Tokens Rule
rules.body: Every repeated size, colour, space, radius, duration or ease comes from a theme token or a documented CSS variable. A one-off stays local and is named in the checkpoint decisions.

dos: Do keep the chosen accent to state and the wordmark; if it is not saying selected, focused or primary action, it is the wrong color.
Do use mono for keys, ids, counts, timestamps and labels, and tabular numerals for every number.
Do separate rows and sections with 1px hairlines and spacing, not cards or shadows.
Do name the next action in empty states and errors, in the product's own language.
Do keep the signed-out margin notes factual: they describe what the files and schema are.
donts: Don't introduce shadows, glass, gradients, glows or colored side stripes.
Don't fill large surfaces with the accent or introduce a second accent.
Don't use emoji as interface icons; they belong only to user-authored space icons.
Don't turn the index into a card grid, add a sidebar before the space exists, or hide the create action behind a modal.
Don't set prose in mono or identifiers in sans.
